attempts.observed: A disposable App Server thread/start returned a non-ephemeral thread id, but after the server exited a second server rejected thread/resume because no rollout existed. A corrected retry wrote one task-owned goal through thread/goal/set without a turn; the next server resumed the thread, read the same goal state and later deleted the thread successfully.

attempts.observed: The disposable native marketplace and plugin lifecycle installed and enabled exact v3.1.0 candidate bytes; source and installed Hook plus runtime SHA-256 values matched. hooks/list discovered the candidate with zero discovery errors. After task-owned goal state made the thread resumable, thread/resume acknowledged successfully but emitted zero hook/started and zero hook/completed notifications. Current official Codex source queues pending SessionStart sources and dispatches them only with a TurnContext, so resume alone restores state but does not execute the Hook before the next turn.
attempts.claimLimit: Exact installed-package zero-turn resume discovery and non-execution only. This does not disprove first-turn resume execution; testing that would start a model turn and crosses a separate cost and data boundary.

No turn result or Agent item was observed, and the task thread plus disposable root were removed.

attempts.observed: One authorized gpt-5.6-luna low-effort synthetic turn ran in an empty disposable cwd over exact installed Hook and runtime bytes. attempts.observed: Current official Codex source defines bypass_hook_trust as a runtime-only ConfigOverrides field. App Server extracts it from the generic thread request config map and supplies it through the typed runtime override while building the session. Passing the same text only as an app-server CLI -c override did not create the required request-scoped trust grant. Generated current-host ThreadStartParams and ThreadResumeParams both expose a config object for that override.
attempts.claimLimit: This corrected probe orchestration and opened, but did not itself satisfy, the separately authorized model-call boundary.

preflightDecision.admitted: A shared short-lived event adapter is feasible and packageable without a persistent process or durable state. One Claude session-only startup event triggered the exact copied adapter and completed silently. One isolated ephemeral Codex thread triggered the reviewed sessionFlags adapter through official compact, injected typed context and produced one matching schema-field Agent response with zero tool use while the installed Hook was disabled. A disposable App Server lane proved that task-owned goal state can make a zero-turn thread resumable and that the official resume response can directly trigger current structured re-sensing, a five-field receipt and pure-core invocation; the core correctly held unknown without independent consequence evidence. The first installed-package turn was retained as an enabled-but-untrusted NO_CONTEXT control. After two pre-model client corrections, the separately authorized request-scoped trust-bypass arm then emitted exactly one installed SessionStart:resume start/completion pair, injected schema/source context and produced exact HOOK_CONTEXT_RESUME with zero tools. Cleanup passed for every task thread, process, root and temporary script.
unknown: installed-package compact and sessionFlags resume execution without the test-only broad trust bypass
whether direct App Server resume-response handling or a first-turn Hook is the lower-burden selected event-to-core route
Agent use beyond one injected schema/source branch
whether an App Server client, bundled MCP, another official carrier or no added product form wins whole-system selection
Node availability across every supported installation surface
Claude compact or resume behavior and cross-host equivalence
preflightDecision.blockedBy: The direct App Server client closes resume-response-to-current-state-to-core connectivity without a model turn. The corrected installed-package Hook arm now closes first-turn resume trigger-to-typed-context-to-one Agent branch only under a broad request-scoped test bypass. Neither arm yet closes the same end-to-end obligation: the direct client lacks selected product form and independent consequence, while the Hook arm lacks official-state re-sensing, pure-core invocation, named consequence and a narrow production trust lifecycle. GT-21 must next compare their total burden under one consequence/interference/continuity/lifecycle oracle, retain a silent sufficient route and prove genuinely independent post-state before MCP, persistence or deeper form is admitted.
